title: Command and Politics in the War Between Moscow and Kyiv
gist: A War on the Rocks podcast with Dara Massicot and Michael Kofman surveys the Russia-Ukraine war: an increasingly fluid battlefield, drones and air defense, the Black Sea campaign, the firing of Ukraine's popular defense minister, doubts that Ukraine can produce PAC-3 missiles, and the likelihood of a new round of Russian mobilization.

insights.claim: Analysts describe the Russia-Ukraine battlefield as increasingly fluid, with drones and air defense and a biting Black Sea campaign as key features of the current phase.
insights.speaker: Dara Massicot, Michael Kofman, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: A more fluid front and intensified Black Sea campaign shift where drone, air-defense, and maritime-strike demand concentrates.
insights.quote: the increasing fluidity of the battlefield, drones and air defense, the biting Black Sea campaign
insights.locator: the increasing fluidity of the battlefield

insights.claim: The analysts argue Ukraine probably cannot produce PAC-3 air defense missiles, contradicting claims made by some journalists.
insights.speaker: Dara Massicot, Michael Kofman, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: Undercuts a narrative of Ukrainian air-defense self-sufficiency, keeping reliance on U.S./allied interceptor supply chains in focus.
insights.quote: why Ukraine probably cannot produce PAC-3 air defense missiles (despite what some journalists are telling you)
insights.locator: why Ukraine probably cannot produce PAC-3

insights.claim: Ukraine's popular defense minister was fired, and the causes and aftermath of that dismissal are treated as a significant political development in the war.
insights.speaker: Dara Massicot, Michael Kofman, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: Turnover in Ukraine's defense leadership can affect procurement continuity and Western coordination.
insights.quote: the causes and aftermath of the firing of Ukraine’s popular defense minister
insights.locator: the firing of Ukraine’s popular defense minister

insights.claim: The analysts assess that a new round of Russian mobilization is likely.
insights.speaker: Dara Massicot, Michael Kofman, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: A fresh mobilization would signal Russian intent to sustain or intensify the war, with implications for war duration and manpower attrition.
insights.quote: the likelihood of a new round of Russian mobilization
insights.locator: the likelihood of a new round of Russian mobilization
